summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure, was admitted after a fall down stairs, sustaining multiple right rib fractures, a pulmonary contusion, and a lumbar spine fracture. He developed acute kidney injury likely due to contrast exposure and volume depletion, leading to toxic-metabolic encephalopathy. He required temporary hemodialysis via a right internal jugular catheter, which was removed after renal recovery. A Citrobacter koseri infection in the transplanted kidney was treated with ceftriaxone followed by oral ciprofloxacin. His mental status improved with dialysis and infection treatment. His pain was managed conservatively, and he was weaned off narcotics. He completed adjustments to his immunosuppressive, anticoagulant, and insulin regimens. He was discharged to an extended care facility with a vancomycin taper for recurrent C. diff, follow-up plans for fecal transplant, and instructions to monitor kidney function and INR.
